46: ✦You may feel very emotional this week.✦You may develop aversions to some foods.✦Or you may strongly crave others.
47: ✦From this week, nausea is hard to avoid for some mothers-to-be.✦A few tips to get through it: – avoid fatty foods, – eat small, frequent meals, – nibble a lightly salted cracker before getting out of bed, – try peppermint tea.
48: ✦In these weeks you may react very emotionally.✦You might burst into tears over something tiny or accuse your partner and loved ones of not understanding you.✦Even though it's hormonal, it may worry the people around you.✦After such moments, telling them it's because of the pregnancy can bring them a lot of relief.
49: ✦From the seventh week, some mothers-to-be develop strong cravings for certain foods.✦These cravings are usually the result of hormonal changes.✦They may also happen when the body needs a vitamin or mineral it's missing.✦They're more common in mothers-to-be with severe nausea who've had to avoid certain foods.✦Cravings can also be a way of seeking attention when a mother-to-be doesn't get enough care from her partner and family.✦Whatever the reason, don't ignore your body's wishes – if possible (in season and available), eat the food you crave.
50: ✦Two-thirds of mothers-to-be have pregnancy nausea at some point in the first trimester.
51: ✦Zinc supports the body at the cellular level.✦It plays a role in building, dividing and protecting cells and in strengthening the immune system.✦It also benefits development, reproduction and bone health.
52: ✦Your doctor may suggest stopping folic acid supplements this week.✦That's because the development of the channel housing the baby's brain and spinal cord (the neural tube) is complete by now.
54: ✦At this stage, the job of the hormone responsible for the lining where the baby is settled passes from the ovary to the placenta, which nourishes the baby.✦During this handover, some mothers-to-be have light spotting.
55: ✦Around the dates of your usual period, you may have cramp-like pains similar to period pain and sometimes even light spotting.✦Even though this is common for some pregnant women, if you have bleeding at 8 weeks, tell your doctor without delay.
56: ✦Until the end of the first trimester, the baby fits inside the pelvis, and this makes you need to pee often.✦In early pregnancy the bladder sits in front of and slightly below the uterus.✦So as the uterus grows, it presses on the bladder.
57: ✦The most noticeable change in the mother this week is the growing uterus.✦Your uterus has reached the size of a medium orange.✦It still sits behind the pubic bone.✦The main reason the uterus grows is the increase in blood circulation in your body.✦Especially in the first 3 months, about 25% of the blood leaving the heart goes to the uterus and placenta.
58: ✦This week, due to increased blood volume, your veins may start to look more visible.✦At 9 weeks, the extra blood volume may also cause occasional nosebleeds.
59: ✦Having more blood in your body also protects you against blood loss during birth.✦The nipples keep darkening and growing.
60: ✦Your kidneys working harder and the uterus pressing on your bladder may make you need to pee often.
61: ✦At 9 weeks, nausea may still be intense for some mothers-to-be.✦Here are the causes of pregnancy nausea.✦A rise in the pregnancy hormone beta-hCG.✦This hormone starts to decline later in the first trimester.✦That's why nausea passes for many women between weeks 13 and 15.✦Sudden drops in blood sugar.✦That's why nausea is often worse when you wake up on an empty stomach.✦Nausea can also appear before other meals as blood sugar drops.✦Rising progesterone relaxes the stomach muscles and slows food moving into the intestines.✦This can increase stomach acid and therefore nausea.✦In cases of excessive vomiting, you may need to be hospitalised and given IV fluids to replace lost water, salt and sugar.
62: ✦In the ninth week, some mothers-to-be may develop skin problems.✦Drinking plenty of water, eating healthily and using gentle, natural skincare can help.✦Remember that mood swings are temporary.✦Enjoy growing your baby day by day.✦Darkening of the genital area is also a sign of 9 weeks of pregnancy.✦Your vaginal discharge may increase.✦If the discharge is yellow, smells bad or itches, tell your doctor.✦Keep eating protein regularly at this stage.✦Your calcium needs are also high now.✦Aim for 1,000–1,500 mg of calcium a day from food.✦If you can't drink milk, have cheese, yogurt or kefir.✦Avoid junk food, fast food and sugary foods.✦Satisfy your sweet tooth with fruit and naturally dried fruit.✦Well-washed salads and lightly cooked vegetables are great sources of vitamin C.✦When buying packaged food, including bread, read labels carefully and limit products with many additives and preservatives.✦Choose fresh, natural foods as much as possible.
63: ✦This week some mothers-to-be may have a small amount of vaginal bleeding.✦It may not be anything bad, but you should still tell your doctor.
64: ✦Your uterus is now the size of a grapefruit – twice its size before pregnancy.✦If this is your first baby, your belly probably isn't showing yet.✦You're probably feeling very tired.
65: ✦At your next prenatal check-up, you may hear your baby's fast heartbeat with a Doppler.✦Your usual clothes may be getting tight; your breasts in particular may no longer fit your bra.✦This might be the week to start wearing maternity clothes.
66: ✦Your belly keeps growing from both bloating and slight weight gain.✦Comfortable clothes with elastic waistbands will make your day easier.✦Depending on how sporty you are, you can do many activities.✦Swimming and walking are ideal choices throughout pregnancy.
67: ✦Exercise is good for your stamina, muscles and strength.✦These help you carry the weight you gain, cope with physical stress and lose weight more easily after birth.
68: ✦Iron, food for the brain, is one of the most important nutrients in a healthy pregnancy diet.✦Iron carries oxygen in your blood.✦Your baby needs iron for cognitive development.
69: ✦Getting enough iron helps carry oxygen in your blood and supports haemoglobin production.✦Healthy red blood cells reduce your risk of anaemia.✦Anaemia, sometimes called iron deficiency, makes you feel tired, worn out and weak.
70: ✦Combining iron-rich foods with sources of vitamin C helps your body absorb iron best.✦Fruit and freshly squeezed juices are ideal for vitamin C.✦Your iron levels will be checked regularly during pregnancy.✦But if you feel exhausted or tired, tell your doctor.✦You may need a supplement for a while.
71: ✦This week your uterus is about the size of a medium grapefruit.✦Your doctor can feel its size by pressing gently on your belly just above the pubic bone.
72: ✦As the uterus rises into the abdomen, pressure on the bladder eases, so you may need to pee less often. At 11 weeks, as the uterus grows, the ligaments on the sides may stretch and you may feel muscle aches.
73: ✦By the end of this week you may feel a bit more relaxed.✦Of course, this differs between mothers-to-be.✦Tiredness may ease.✦You may feel more energetic.✦Your breasts may have grown 2–3 sizes, but after the eleventh week their growth slows.✦They may grow a little more in the last month.
74: ✦Signs at this stage may include headaches, decreased or increased sex drive, sleep problems and skin issues such as stretch marks.
75: ✦Constipation is one of the most common signs at this stage.✦The main reason is the growing uterus pressing on the intestines and slowing them down.✦Eat plenty of high-fibre foods.✦Include beans and lentils.✦Dried fruit is a good choice too.✦Since fibre can cause gas and bloating, spread these foods across your meals.✦Try to drink plenty of fluids.✦Compote made from dried fruit is also very effective.✦If constipation continues despite all this, talk to your doctor and follow their advice.
76: ✦Within a few weeks after this week, you should have the 11–14 week screening (the combined or double test).✦This test checks the nuchal translucency on ultrasound to assess the risk of Down syndrome.✦This screening is very important; ask your doctor about it.
77: ✦Since iron supplements can cause constipation, eat plenty of vegetables and salads.✦Don't rely only on supplements – try to eat foods like eggs, meat and spinach in a balanced way every day.✦Take your iron supplement a few hours before or after calcium-rich foods.✦Otherwise less iron is absorbed.
78: ✦Drink fluids between meals rather than with them.✦Eat smaller, easily digestible portions.✦Chew your food well.✦Avoid spicy foods, sour juices, coffee and chocolate.✦When lying down, keep your head and chest higher than the rest of your body.✦Eat dinner early so your body has time to digest.
79: ✦You're almost at the end of this month of pregnancy.✦This week your uterus is the size of a large grapefruit.✦As your uterus grows, it's normal to feel occasional aches in your sides.
80: ✦Here's one positive change this week: since your uterus has moved up a little since last week, you'll feel some relief on your bladder.✦You should have the 11–14 week screening within a few weeks.✦This test measures your baby's nuchal translucency.
81: ✦For some women, nausea and tiredness may almost disappear.✦They may be replaced by a feeling of renewed energy.✦If your blood type is Rh negative and your partner's is Rh positive, there may be some issues in pregnancy and for your baby.✦Your doctor will give you the necessary treatment during pregnancy and after birth.
82: ✦If you didn't start last week, you may need to start iron supplements at 12 weeks – ask your doctor. Otherwise you may become anaemic, which can make you feel weak. Iron supplements also help protect against heavy bleeding at birth.
83: ✦If your breasts are sore this week, applying an organic nipple cream (which you can also use after birth) to the whole breast every day may bring relief.✦Don't apply it for too long.✦A long, massage-like application can stimulate the breasts, which may trigger contractions.
84: ✦From this week you may tire quickly and get out of breath.✦This is because your body needs more oxygen.✦Exercise may trigger it.✦Remember to rest and take short breaks.
85: ✦Although your baby's birth is months away, your breasts and milk ducts are preparing for breastfeeding.✦Soon they'll start producing a fluid called colostrum.✦This fluid is full of nutrients and will be your baby's first milk.
86: ✦As your breasts grow, they get heavier and firmer.✦Although underwire bras haven't been proven harmful, many experts suggest wire-free bras for now, as they may restrict natural breast changes and the developing milk ducts.
87: ✦Next week the second trimester begins and your early pregnancy symptoms will ease.
88: ✦This week your gums may keep bleeding.✦Brushing your teeth regularly will help.✦Ask your dentist which toothpaste is best for you during pregnancy.✦Keeping up good dental habits for life – and teaching them to your child – is important for health.✦Don't hesitate to get any treatment your dentist recommends if needed.✦Dental treatments are done safely during pregnancy today.
89: ✦Drink plenty of water.✦Take your iron supplements regularly.✦Pay attention to your diet.✦Try not to overeat.✦About 300 extra calories a day is enough.✦With twins, it should be 500–600 extra calories a day. Eat plenty of protein- and calcium-rich foods every day in a balanced way.✦To prevent cramps, eat magnesium-rich foods like bananas.
90: ✦Try not to gain too much weight.✦In the first 3 months, women typically gain only about 1–2 kg.✦In the second and third trimesters, gain is usually around 0.4–0.5 kg per week, depending on your starting weight; your doctor will advise you. Gaining too much can make the baby larger and raises the risk of gestational diabetes, so aim for steady, moderate gain rather than eating for two.
91: ✦At 13 weeks, start thinking about antenatal classes.✦If you're going with your partner, registering early helps you secure suitable dates.✦Antenatal classes differ in content.✦Some focus on baby care.✦These are useful for preparing to be parents.✦But to really prepare for birth, it helps to choose birth-focused classes that teach things useful during labour.✦Such classes can help you and your partner overcome fear of birth.✦And have a healthy, positive birth.
92: ✦You've now left the first trimester behind.✦The risk of miscarriage is now much lower.✦About three-quarters of miscarriages happen in the first 3 months.✦At 14 weeks, the belly becomes more visible.
93: ✦The discomforts of the first period are easing and your energy is coming back.✦Morning sickness and the need to pee are decreasing.✦You can start buying maternity clothes, because now it's clear you're expecting.
94: ✦Although you feel much better than at first, you may still feel exhausted now and then.✦Your blood pressure may drop.✦Constipation may continue.
95: ✦Feeling stuffy? This is called pregnancy rhinitis, and progesterone is to blame.✦It increases circulation to the mucous membranes of the nose, making them swell.✦There aren't many treatments, but a humidifier, warm compress or a little petroleum jelly around the nostrils may help.✦Avoid medicated nasal sprays unless your doctor approves.
